about.heading: About Cosmosyy
about.challengeDesc: This project was created for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge, responding to the prompt: Abandoned but Not Forgotten — Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment.
about.whatWeBuiltDesc: Cosmosyy is an interactive 3D experience that lets you explore authentic landing sites and flight trajectories across Apollo Moon missions, Mars rover sites, and deep-space probes. You discover the heritage objects — scientific instruments, rovers, descent stages, and personal items — that humanity left behind across the cosmos.
about.whyWeBuilt: Why We Built It This Way
about.whyWeBuiltSubtitle: Direct choices addressing the NASA Space Apps Challenge considerations
about.designAgeGroupDesc: Built for school-age explorers (roughly ages 10-16) and curious adults — every object has two narration tracks: a plain first-person 'Kids' story and a cited 'Explorer' technical track, switchable anytime.
about.designAccessibilityDesc: Runs offline, in English and Hindi, with captions, reduced motion, and keyboard-only play; a lightweight non-3D fallback renders the same story for low-end devices or screen readers.
about.designScopeDesc: We chose breadth over depth: all six Apollo landing sites plus nine Mars missions and five deep-space probes, so the player sees the full range of what 'abandoned NASA hardware' actually means, from a parked Moon buggy to a probe still drifting past the edge of the solar system.
about.designPerspectiveDesc: Every artifact speaks in first person — a 'Dormant Voice Log' — so the hardware tells its own story, with a toggle to switch to NASA's own technical catalog data for the parts of the audience who want the hard numbers.
about.nasaDataDesc: Every fact, coordinate, and artifact in this game comes from verified NASA sources. Landing coordinates use LROC/HiRISE data. Heritage object descriptions reference NASA mission archives, ALSEP documentation, and JPL mission pages.
about.heritagePreservationDesc: The Artemis Accords (Section 9) recognize Apollo landing sites as historically significant. NASA's 2011 recommendations establish exclusion zones around Apollo 11 and 17 sites. These artifacts are humanity's first archaeological record on another world — they deserve protection and remembrance.
